market.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (research/educational use; see docs/dataset_notes.md)

execution_rules.timing: each session's action is decided pre-open and filled at that session's open; the portfolio is marked to market at that session's close

actions.buy: open a long position only when flat; invest position_fraction of current equity, whole shares only

execution_rules.position_limit: long-only, one position, no pyramiding, no shorting
execution_rules.sizing: position_fraction=1.0 of equity at the fill price, capped by available cash including the transaction cost; unaffordable sizes are reduced, and zero affordable shares means no trade
execution_rules.costs: transaction_cost_bps=10.0 charged on the traded notional of both buys and sells
execution_rules.idealisation: no slippage, partial fills, liquidity limits, taxes, or dividends; close is the raw (unadjusted) close

checks.name: sessions_chronological_and_unique
checks.detail: sessions arrive in ascending order with unique dates; the simulator never reorders rows

checks.name: prices_complete_and_positive
checks.detail: every session has a positive open and close; nothing is filled

checks.name: buy_and_hold_enters_once
checks.detail: the buy-and-hold benchmark executes exactly one trade

checks.name: benchmarks_cover_every_session
checks.detail: each strategy produces one equity row per session

checks.name: replay_is_deterministic
checks.detail: re-running identical prices and actions yields identical cash, shares and portfolio values

checks.name: maximum_drawdown_in_unit_interval

limitations: Historical simulation only: this is not a forecast and does not establish future profitability.
One instrument, whole shares, one position, long-only: no portfolio construction or risk limits beyond position_fraction.
Fills occur at the open with no slippage or liquidity model; real execution would be worse.
The transaction cost is a flat bps of notional on both sides; market impact and spread are not modelled separately.
Raw close is used, so dividends and any unadjusted corporate actions are ignored.
Momentum and buy-and-hold are benchmarks for later comparison, not recommended strategies.
